cf.title: Fall back to serial vacuum when out of DSM segments

input.subject: Parallel autovacuum: leader crashes when no DSM segment can be created

verdict_reasoning: No fundamental objection survived for HEAD. The fallback copies what parallel index builds do, adds no user-visible surface, and costs nothing for users who do not run parallel vacuum. The one surviving objection, demand-1, is fixable and bears mostly on the "stable" target, which the thread does not argue. A committer who knows parallel vacuum must decide on the backpatch and on removing the nworkers check from cc053b6e127.

brief.title: Fall back to serial vacuum when parallel vacuum gets no DSM segment
brief.problem: When all DSM slots are taken, VACUUM (PARALLEL 2) fails with "too many dynamic shared memory segments", while VACUUM (PARALLEL 0) succeeds. InitializeParallelDSM() already falls back to a leader-only context, but parallel vacuum then creates a shared TidStore that needs another DSM segment. This affects manual parallel vacuum and parallel autovacuum.
brief.proposed_design: When pcxt->seg is NULL, parallel_vacuum_init() returns NULL, so the caller uses a local TidStore and vacuums serially, like parallel index builds do. The patch also removes the nworkers check added by the crash fix cc053b6e127, which the author thinks becomes redundant.
user_visible_surface: VACUUM (PARALLEL n) and parallel autovacuum finish serially instead of failing when no DSM segment is free at context setup.
author_claims: The shared TidStore in the no-worker case defeats the leader-only fallback from InitializeParallelDSM().
Parallel index builds already back out in the same way.
The nworkers check from cc053b6e127 becomes redundant with this change.
brief.thread_state: The crash fix (v1 from message #1) was pushed as cc053b6e127; this entry is the follow-up. Bharath objects that a later dead-TID DSM allocation can still fail, so failing is fine, but supports pursuing it for HEAD; shihao zhong says v1 still fixes the all-slots-taken case and suggests reserving DSM slots for vacuum.
unclear: The CommitFest entry is tagged Bugfix with target "stable", but the thread only discusses HEAD; the backpatch intent is not stated.
The proposal does not say what happens when a later dead-TID DSM allocation fails after the parallel context got a segment.
The material gives no reproducer or test for the new fallback path.
The proposal does not say whether the serial fallback is logged or reported to the user.

objections.title: No field report of DSM exhaustion breaking parallel vacuum
objections.failure_scenario: A committer pushes the fallback, possibly to stable branches as the CommitFest target suggests. No user who reported the error exists to confirm that it helps. Users who do run out of DSM slots, and still have one slot left, still see "too many dynamic shared memory segments" from the dead-TID allocation.
objections.argument: The only evidence is a synthetic test in message #4, where another session holds every DSM slot. Message #7 calls DSM exhaustion very rare and says the reviewer had never seen it. Message #6 says the error is acceptable because it can happen anyway, and message #7 agrees that the one-slot-left case still fails. So the fix covers a narrow case with no reported users. The change is small, but a Bugfix tag with target "stable" needs more than a synthetic case.
objections.author_must_show: Which production systems have seen parallel vacuum or parallel autovacuum fail with "too many dynamic shared memory segments", and would the all-slots-taken fallback have covered them?

critic.reasoning: The thread shows only a synthetic case, message #7 calls DSM exhaustion very rare, and the "stable" target is not argued anywhere. For HEAD the objection is weak: the fallback copies parallel index builds, adds no user-visible surface, and costs non-users nothing.

questions: Is this change meant for HEAD only, or for backpatch to 19 as the "stable" target on the CommitFest entry suggests?
Which production systems have seen parallel vacuum or parallel autovacuum fail with "too many dynamic shared memory segments", and would the all-slots-taken fallback have covered them?
What happens when the parallel context gets a segment but the later dead-TID DSM allocation fails: does vacuum still raise the error, and is that accepted?
Which case did the nworkers check from cc053b6e127 cover, and why can it not occur once parallel_vacuum_init() returns NULL for a NULL pcxt->seg?
Does vacuum log or report that it fell back to serial because no DSM segment was free?

committability.owner_note: Masahiko Sawada pushed the related crash fix in message #3. The follow-up needs a committer who knows parallel vacuum and the DSM fallback in InitializeParallelDSM().
committability.liability: The owner signs for parallel vacuum and parallel autovacuum behaviour under DSM exhaustion, including the removal of the guard from cc053b6e127. A backpatch extends that to the stable branch for its lifetime.
committability.author_follow_up: The author created the CommitFest entry on 2026-10-01 and renamed it on 2026-10-21. The visible messages show no other sign either way.

priority.reason: The thread shows DSM exhaustion only in a synthetic test, so few users benefit. The change is local to parallel_vacuum_init() and follows the existing parallel index build fallback; the follow-up patch itself was not read.

provisional_note: The follow-up patch and messages #4 to #7 were not shown. Without the code, it is not possible to confirm that removing the nworkers check is safe or that every caller handles a NULL return from parallel_vacuum_init().

precedents_retrieved.title: DSA Hash Tables (DHT): hash tables backed by DSM segments
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a general-purpose hash table in DSA memory, so several backends can share it and it can grow, along the lines of dynahash. It uses separate chaining, incremental resizing, partition-based locking and concurrent iteration.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author parked the patch after its only planned user, Dilip Kumar's Parallel Bitmap Heap Scan, stopped using it. He did not expect a committer to take it without a concrete user, which Andres Freund had asked for at the start. Reviewers found no problems with the design.

precedents_retrieved.title: Block level parallel vacuum
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds parallel workers to VACUUM: each worker scans a range of heap blocks, collects dead tuple locations and reclaims them, and the leader gathers the statistics and updates relfrozenxid. Later versions added progress reporting and a per-table parallel degree for autovacuum.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier returned the patch in November 2017 because it depended on a separate extension lock patch, and he proposed coming back once those root problems were addressed. A regression failure ("cache lookup failed for relation" from DROP SCHEMA ... CASCADE) was also still unexplained. The first round in 2016 was returned for lack of activity, after early tests showed index vacuum slowing down with more workers because of cleanup lock contention on index buffers.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
So I propose to mark this patch as
returned with feedback for now, and come back to it once the root
problems are addressed.

precedents_retrieved.title: Autovacuum dynamic cost_limit, cost_delay
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes autovac_balance_cost() so that a running autovacuum worker's cost limit is capped at a new MAXVACUUMCOSTLIMIT constant (10000) instead of at wi_cost_limit_base. This lets a reload of autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit or autovacuum_vacuum_cost_delay speed up vacuums that are already running.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Masahiko Sawada argued that the cap at wi_cost_limit_base guards against roundoff errors, so raising it to the maximum could set a worker's limit higher than its base value without need. He said the real problem is that wi_cost_limit_base and wi_cost_delay are not updated when the cost is rebalanced, and proposed a different direction that would drop wi_cost_limit_base. The visible messages show no revised patch after his last reply.

precedents_retrieved.title: Shared-memory based stats collector
precedents_retrieved.summary: Replace the file-based stats collector with statistics kept in dynamic shared memory (dshash), so backends read stats without a stats file written by a separate process. The stats collector process goes away, and per-kind stats code moves into new files under utils/activity.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund reworked the patch in spring 2021 and judged it not committable for v14, citing weak test coverage, the need for architectural review and performance testing, an unresolved case where stats for dropped functions can be revived, and many open FIXMEs. A rebase then stalled on a new issue with partitioned tables. No new version was posted after July 2021, so the CommitFest manager marked the entry Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Block level parallel vacuum
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Robert Haas, Claudio Freire, Michael Paquier, Pavan Deolasee
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch parallelizes VACUUM by giving each worker a fixed range of heap blocks, for which the worker collects dead tuples and then vacuums both the heap and all indexes. It also changes buffer locking so that several processes can wait for a cleanup lock, and adds a vacuum_parallel_workers GUC.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers rejected the design because each worker scans every index, which adds index scanning work and makes workers contend for cleanup locks on the same index pages; the author's own benchmark showed index vacuum getting slower with more workers. Robert Haas proposed a parallel heap scan with a shared dead tuple array and one worker per index, and the author agreed. While reworking the patch, the author hit an unsolved problem: parallel workers in one lock group can extend the FSM or VM at the same time and fail. The entry was then closed for lack of activity after the feedback was given.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This doesn't seem like a good design, because it adds a lot of extra
index scanning work.

precedents_retrieved.title: Block level parallel vacuum
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets VACUUM use several worker processes, each scanning a block range of the heap for dead tuples, with the leader then collecting the results and updating relfrozenxid. It also lets several processes wait for a cleanup lock on one buffer, and it adds a vacuum_parallel_workers GUC.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas proposed moving the patch to v11 because it still had too many open issues for the rest of the cycle, among them deadlock problems that need careful changes. The patch was also not in reviewable shape by March 1st. The author agreed that the design needed more discussion, and David Steele marked it Returned with Feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think there are
too many issues here to address in the limited time we have remaining
this cycle, and I believe that if we try to get them all solved in the
next few weeks we're likely to end up getting backed into some choices
by time pressure that we may later regret bitterly.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fallback table AM for relkinds without storage
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a fallback table AM whose callbacks all raise an error, and assign it to relkinds without storage (views, foreign tables, partitioned tables) so that rd_tableam is never NULL. A wrong call into the table AM API for such a relation would then raise an error instead of crashing the backend.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund objected that the patch moves relkind-specific logic, such as choosing the slot type, into an AM that should never be called. He suggested separate AMs instead, for example one for foreign tables and one for sequences. Michael Paquier agreed he was not comfortable passing relkind knowledge into the AM, and he returned the entry because he was not sure what the right design was.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This doesn't seem like an advantage to me. Isn't this just pushing logic
away from a fairly obvious point into an AM that one would expect to
never actually get called?

precedents_retrieved.title: Use AF_UNIX for tests on Windows (ie drop fallback TCP code)
precedents_retrieved.summary: Thomas Munro proposed using AF_UNIX sockets for pg_regress and TAP tests on Windows too, removing the Windows-only TCP and SSPI setup code in the test harness. To match Unix security, mkdtemp() on Windows would create the socket directory with access for the current user only.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that with TCP gone from the Windows tests, the TCP socket code would have little test coverage on any platform, and reviewers asked for a switch that runs the tests over either TCP or Unix sockets. The author agreed, set the TAP test patch aside for more work and posted only the first two patches. Those later stopped applying, the author posted no new version, and the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
If we remove that, won't we have a whole lot of code that's not
tested at all on any platform, ie all the TCP-socket code?

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert recent change to RequestNamedLWLockTranche().
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert recent change to RequestNamedLWLockTranche().
Reverted commit(s): Move dynamically-allocated LWLock tranche names to shared memory.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Commit 38b602b028 modified this function to allocate enough space
for MAX_NAMED_TRANCHES (256) requests, which is likely far more
than most clusters need.  This commit reverts that change so that
it first allocates enough space for only 16 requests and resizes
the array when necessary.  While at it, remove the check for too
many tranches from this function.  We can now rely on
InitializeLWLocks() to do that check via its calls to
LWLockNewTrancheId() for the named tranches.

precedents_retrieved.objection:
This commit reverts the work done by commits 3ba59ccc89 and 72e78d831a.
Those commits were incorrect in asserting that we never acquire any other
heavy-weight lock after acquring page lock other than relation extension
lock. We can acquire a lock on catalogs while doing catalog look up after
acquring page lock.

This won't impact any existing feature but we need to think some other way
to achieve this before parallelizing other write operations or even
improving the parallelism in vacuum (like allowing multiple workers
for an index).

precedents_retrieved.summary:

precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit aa607980aee08416211f003ab41aa750f5559712.

This test proved to be unstable on the buildfarm, timing out before the
standby could catch up on 32-bit machines where more rows were required
and failing to reliably trigger multiple index vacuum rounds on 64-bit
machines where fewer rows should be required.

Because the instability is only known to be present on versions of
Postgres with TIDStore used for dead TID storage by vacuum, this is only
being reverted on master and REL_17_STABLE.

As having this coverage may be valuable, there is a discussion on the
thread of possible ways to stabilize the test. If that happens, a fixed
test can be committed again.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the index returned no earlier rejected, returned or reverted proposal on this idea. Inside the thread, the only earlier work is the crash fix from message #1, pushed in message #3. That fix complements this proposal and was not rejected, and the open concern in message #6 belongs to the design angle.

No standards or compatibility objection holds up. The proposal adds no syntax, GUC, catalog object or dump state, and it turns an error into the leader-only fallback that InitializeParallelDSM() already offers and that VACUUM (PARALLEL) documents, since fewer workers than requested is normal. The "stable" target and whether the fallback is reported are open questions, but neither gives a concrete failure for existing users.

The proposal touches no persistent or cross-node state: no on-disk format, WAL, catalog, wire protocol or exported signature changes. DSM segments are transient shared memory, and choosing a local TidStore over a shared one does not affect replication, pg_upgrade or the extension ABI.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. It changes only whether VACUUM (PARALLEL n) and parallel autovacuum fail or fall back to serial when DSM slots run out, and that fallback makes an existing unprivileged way of using up DSM slots less harmful.

No maintenance or fit objection holds. The change is local to parallel_vacuum_init(), copies the existing leader-only fallback that parallel index builds use, and adds no cost for anyone who does not run parallel vacuum. Two questions are left to other angles: whether removing the nworkers guard from cc053b6e127 is safe, and whether the fix is incomplete because a later dead-TID DSM allocation can still fail (message #6).

Postgres has no existing way to meet this need. A user can rerun with VACUUM (PARALLEL 0), but parallel autovacuum has no such retry. The patch also does not add a new mechanism: it makes the existing leader-only fallback in InitializeParallelDSM() reach vacuum, as parallel index builds already do.
One demand objection. The change itself is small and costs non-users almost nothing, so this is a "not now, show demand" point for the stable target, and the case for HEAD is weaker.
